{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABY1tLyg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhCbRgk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 5, "title": "Complete the remaining first-playable SNES release requirements from #3", "body": "## Problem

This is the successor completion tracker for [Issue #3](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/3). The owner requested closing #3 and moving its unfinished work into a new actionable Issue. Closing #3 is a tracking transition, not a claim that its original delivery is complete.

[PR #4](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/4) merged the initial implementation as `4c073d47ff7b50b476284b660b52f12c487c3648`. Preserve that work: the Rust core, native runner, Wasm/browser app, cleared game builds, gameplay/audio/SRAM regressions, and CI already exist. Start from current `main`; do not rebuild the project from scratch.

The final review reported passing first-playable acceptance, but the merged PR, README and [delivery checklist](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-3-progress.md) still describe required timing, PPU and audio work as incomplete. The closing node therefore left #3 open. Resolve this discrepancy against implementation and executable evidence, and complete the genuine remaining requirements.

## Expected outcome

Finish the original first-playable browser SNES release: two distinct, legally cleared actual homebrew games run through the same generic Rust/Wasm core with sustained controller-driven gameplay, game-derived graphics, working music/sound effects and stable audio/video synchronization. All mandatory requirements from #3 must be implemented and verified, with consistent current documentation.

This Issue is the active completion tracker for that delivery. A PR for this Issue must fully resolve its mandatory scope; another partial checkpoint must not be approved or merged as its resolution.

## Remaining work

1. Reconcile every original implementation and pre-merge criterion with current-head code and reproducible evidence. Record which are already satisfied and which still need implementation. Preserve validated work; passing existing tests alone does not establish a missing requirement.
2. Complete the remaining CPU/bus/event-timing behavior needed by the mandatory targets: applicable IRQ/NMI timing, CPU/PPU/DMA/HDMA interactions and memory-access ordering. Add independently expected timing/ordering regressions; the existing CPU semantic suites do not prove timing correctness.
3. Complete or verify PPU behavior used by those targets, including relevant register/latch/access behavior and raster effects. Exercise actual guest-generated framebuffer output with licensed fixtures or original tests. Fix demonstrated missing behavior rather than hiding it in a limitations paragraph.
4. Complete or verify the required audio path beyond non-silent samples: SPC700/DSP behavior needed for target-game music/effects, deterministic sample generation and browser scheduling without uncontrolled audio/video drift or unbounded queues. Add automated numerical and browser checks for relevant DSP/timing gaps; do not treat a running sample counter as proof of correct sound.
5. Resolve the game-selection/provenance concern explicitly. Castle Platformer and modified Memory Game are distinct gameplay programs but share an author/library. Establish source/build provenance and whether the selected pair satisfies #3's independent-game acceptance; author identity alone is not a new gate. If a required acceptance condition is not met, select and audit a suitable legally redistributable alternative and implement its required behavior. Do not waive a criterion merely because the current pair passes. Preserve exact artifact hashes, notices and reproducible source builds; do not rely on unaudited original-release ROMs.
6. Update README, the delivery checklist and validation records to describe the verified final result consistently. Mark only demonstrated mandatory criteria complete, link #3 to this successor tracker, and distinguish optional unsupported hardware from required target behavior. Documentation changes alone cannot replace missing implementation or tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Every original mandatory implementation and acceptance item from #3 maps to current code and reproducible evidence; all remaining agent-fixable gaps are implemented, without weakening the original first-release requirements.
- [ ] At least two distinct, fully audited actual game artifacts boot through the same generic core. Their source/build/asset provenance and selection rationale are recorded, with no emulator-side per-game behavior or unaudited ROMs/assets.
- [ ] Each required game has an automated reset-to-gameplay input replay lasting at least five emulated minutes, with sustained input-derived interactions and changing game-derived frames. Exercise reachable progression/completion where exposed, detect late freezes, and retain explicit frame/wall-clock bounds.
- [ ] At least one selected game has verified game-generated music and sound effects. Automated tests cover relevant DSP outputs and real Web Audio scheduling, finite samples, bounded queues/drift, gesture activation, pause/reset and repeat playback. Timing/PPU regressions cover the required paths identified above.
- [ ] Documented format, lint, Rust tests, Wasm/production build, licensed CPU/SPC700 and PPU/DMA fixtures, reproducible game builds, browser checks and applicable GitHub CI pass on the final implementation. Preserve keyboard/gamepad, local-file privacy, scaling, errors and SRAM persistence/recovery coverage.
- [ ] README, delivery checklist, PR description and validation evidence agree that this Issue's mandatory first-playable release is complete, while accurately listing optional limitations. Review checks both missing requirements and unnecessary scope; remaining fixable mandatory gaps return to implementation, not partial approval.

## Scope and workflow constraints

Use English for new code-facing documentation, Issue/PR text, reviews and commit messages, following the repository's existing development and review guidance. Prefer the smallest complete implementation; avoid speculative abstractions, unrelated refactoring or new frameworks.

This is the first playable baseline from #3, not complete SNES catalog or chip-perfect hardware compatibility. Enhancement chips, PAL, save states, additional PPU modes/mappers and other hardware features are optional unless a mandatory target needs them. Do not add physical-device, subjective listening, proprietary-ROM, live deployment or post-merge confirmation gates. Use automated local/CI evidence. If genuinely indispensable human input is discovered, record the concrete blocker and wait rather than cycling through code fixes.

## Optional validation

Additional games, longer sessions, more browsers, physical gamepads, reference comparisons and lawfully user-supplied commercial ROMs. These do not block the defined first-playable delivery.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Deployment or live-site verification is outside this Issue's mandatory completion conditions.
